output.section: 1. Purpose & Scope / 1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)
output.text:
### 1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)

This SLA governs the operational uptime, availability, and technical support for three core platform systems:

1. Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable virtual compute instances, software-defined virtual private clouds (VPCs), edge load balancers, persistent block storage volumes, and distributed object storage.
2. Managed Database Engine: High-availability managed PostgreSQL clusters and distributed cache nodes, including automated failover, cluster synchronization, and continuous transactional backups.
3. CloudScale API Platform: Public REST API endpoints, GraphQL queries and mutations, incoming/outgoing webhook dispatch engines, and customer identity/authentication microservices.

output.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

output.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

## 1. Purpose & Scope

This Service Level Agreement ("SLA") and Support Tier Policy establishes the binding performance standards, availability commitments, and technical support response standards provided by CloudScale Inc. The objective is to provide clear, measurable operational benchmarks and transparent compensation rules so that organizations running production workloads can plan and operate with complete certainty.

output.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.

output.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
output.text:
### 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy

Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated refunds.

output.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
output.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
output.text:
### 3.4 Non-Refundable Services

The following professional fees and third-party expenses are strictly non-refundable under all circumstances:

- Custom Onboarding & Implementation: Dedicated deployment engineering, custom setup packages, and architecture consulting.
- Domain Registrations & SSL Certificates: Domain purchases, custom SSL certificate procurement, and DNS routing setup fees.
- Data Migration Engineering: Tailored database migration scripts, pipeline development, and dedicated engineering hours.
- Dedicated Technical Account Management (TAM): Monthly retainer fees for designated account managers.

output.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
output.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
output.text:
### 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee

CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:

- Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial service activation date.
- Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50 computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes strictly non-refundable.
- Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

chunks.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
chunks.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
chunks.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

chunks.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.2 Response Time Matrix
chunks.text:
### 5.2 Response Time Matrix

Initial response time is defined as the duration between ticket creation and the first substantive technical response by a qualified CloudScale support engineer.

Table 3: Support Severity Levels and Guaranteed Initial Response Times

| Severity Level        | Operational Impact          | Starter Tier                 | Professional Tier            | Enterprise Tier               |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Severity 1 (Critical) | Total production out- age   | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 2 Hours (24/7/365)         | ≤ 30 Minutes (24/7 Dedicated) |
| Severity 2 (Major)    | Core features impaired      | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 6 Hours (Busi- ness Hours) | ≤ 2 Hours (24/7/365)          |
| Severity 3 (Minor)    | Non-critical defect / bug   | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 24 Hours (Busi- ness Days) | ≤ 12 Hours (24/5 Business)    |
| Severity 4 (Guidance) | General inquiry / re- quest | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 48 Hours (Busi- ness Days) | ≤ 24 Hours (Busi- ness Days)  |

chunks.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
chunks.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
chunks.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

chunks.text:
### 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.
- Enterprise Tier: 24/7/365 dedicated telephone hotline, synchronized Slack/Teams Connect channels, Priority Web Portal, and direct assignment to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) with Tier-3 SRE escalation.

input_chunks.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
input_chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
input_chunks.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

input_chunks.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
input_chunks.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
input_chunks.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

input_chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
input_chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
input_chunks.text:
### 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy

Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated refunds.

input_chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
input_chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
input_chunks.text:
### 3.4 Non-Refundable Services

The following professional fees and third-party expenses are strictly non-refundable under all circumstances:

- Custom Onboarding & Implementation: Dedicated deployment engineering, custom setup packages, and architecture consulting.
- Domain Registrations & SSL Certificates: Domain purchases, custom SSL certificate procurement, and DNS routing setup fees.
- Data Migration Engineering: Tailored database migration scripts, pipeline development, and dedicated engineering hours.
- Dedicated Technical Account Management (TAM): Monthly retainer fees for designated account managers.

input_chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
input_chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
input_chunks.text:
### 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee

CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:

- Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial service activation date.
- Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50 computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes strictly non-refundable.
- Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

### 3.1 Cancellation Submission Process

Clients may initiate subscription cancellation via the CloudScale Admin Console (https://console.cloudscale.io/ billing) or by emailing written notice to billing@cloudscale.io. Cancellation notices must be received at least 48 hours prior to the next billing date.

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. $$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

output.text:
### 1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)

This SLA governs the operational uptime, availability, and technical support for three core platform systems:

1. Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable virtual compute instances, software-defined virtual private clouds (VPCs), edge load balancers, persistent block storage volumes, and distributed object storage.
2. Managed Database Engine: High-availability managed PostgreSQL clusters and distributed cache nodes, including automated failover, cluster synchronization, and continuous transactional backups.
3. CloudScale API Platform: Public REST API endpoints, GraphQL queries and mutations, incoming/outgoing webhook dispatch engines, and customer identity/authentication microservices.

output.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

output.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

This Service Level Agreement ("SLA") and Support Tier Policy establishes the binding performance standards, availability commitments, and technical support response standards provided by CloudScale Inc. The objective is to provide clear, measurable operational benchmarks and transparent compensation rules so that organizations running production workloads can plan and operate with complete certainty.

| Severity Level        | Operational Impact          | Starter Tier                 | Professional Tier            | Enterprise Tier               |

output.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.
- Enterprise Tier: 24/7/365 dedicated telephone hotline, synchronized Slack/Teams Connect channels, Priority Web Portal, and direct assignment to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) with Tier-3 SRE escalation.

### 1.1 Covered Services (In-Scope Components)

This SLA governs the operational uptime, availability, and technical support for three core platform systems:

1. Cloud Infrastructure: Scalable virtual compute instances, software-defined virtual private clouds (VPCs), edge load balancers, persistent block storage volumes, and distributed object storage.
2. Managed Database Engine: High-availability managed PostgreSQL clusters and distributed cache nodes, including automated failover, cluster synchronization, and continuous transactional backups.
3. CloudScale API Platform: Public REST API endpoints, GraphQL queries and mutations, incoming/outgoing webhook dispatch engines, and customer identity/authentication microservices.

output.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

output.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

## 1. Purpose & Scope

This Service Level Agreement ("SLA") and Support Tier Policy establishes the binding performance standards, availability commitments, and technical support response standards provided by CloudScale Inc. ("CloudScale") to its customers. The objective is to provide clear, measurable operational benchmarks and transparent compensation rules so that organizations running production workloads can plan and operate with complete certainty.

output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.2 Response Time Matrix
output.text:
### 5.2 Response Time Matrix

Initial response time is defined as the duration between ticket creation and the first substantive technical response by a qualified CloudScale support engineer.

Table 3: Support Severity Levels and Guaranteed Initial Response Times

| Severity Level        | Operational Impact          | Starter Tier                 | Professional Tier            | Enterprise Tier               |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Severity 1 (Critical) | Total production out- age   | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 2 Hours (24/7/365)         | ≤ 30 Minutes (24/7 Dedicated) |
| Severity 2 (Major)    | Core features impaired      | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 6 Hours (Busi- ness Hours) | ≤ 2 Hours (24/7/365)          |
| Severity 3 (Minor)    | Non-critical defect / bug   | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 24 Hours (Busi- ness Days) | ≤ 12 Hours (24/5 Business)    |
| Severity 4 (Guidance) | General inquiry / re- quest | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 48 Hours (Busi- ness Days) | ≤ 24 Hours (Busi- ness Days)  |

output.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

output.text:
### 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.
- Enterprise Tier: 24/7/365 dedicated telephone hotline, synchronized Slack/Teams Connect channels, Priority Web Portal, and direct assignment to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) with Tier-3 SRE escalation.

chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

chunks.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.2 Service Credit Brackets
chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.2 Service Credit Brackets
chunks.text:
### 4.2 Service Credit Brackets

Service credit percentages are determined by the customer subscription tier and actual monthly uptime achieved:

Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

| Monthly Uptime %                                                                     | Enterprise Credit                                                                               | Professional Credit                                                                              | Application Mechanism                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 99.90% to < 99.99% 99.00% to < 99.90% 98.00% to < 99.00% 95.00% to < 98.00% < 95.00% | 10% of Monthly Fee 25% of Monthly Fee 50% of Monthly Fee 50% of Monthly Fee 100% of Monthly Fee | SLA Target Met (0%) 10% of Monthly Fee 25% of Monthly Fee 50% of Monthly Fee 100% of Monthly Fee | Applied to subsequent billing invoice Applied to subsequent billing invoice Applied to subsequent billing invoice Applied to subsequent billing invoice Maximum allowable monthly credit |

chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments
chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments
chunks.text:
### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

chunks.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
chunks.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

chunks.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
chunks.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
chunks.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
chunks.text:
### 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy

Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated refunds.

chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
chunks.text:
### 3.4 Non-Refundable Services

The following professional fees and third-party expenses are strictly non-refundable under all circumstances:

- Custom Onboarding & Implementation: Dedicated deployment engineering, custom setup packages, and architecture consulting.
- Domain Registrations & SSL Certificates: Domain purchases, custom SSL certificate procurement, and DNS routing setup fees.
- Data Migration Engineering: Tailored database migration scripts, pipeline development, and dedicated engineering hours.
- Dedicated Technical Account Management (TAM): Monthly retainer fees for designated account managers.

chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
chunks.text:
### 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee

CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:

- Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial service activation date.
- Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50 computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes strictly non-refundable.
- Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

chunks.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.1 Cancellation Submission Process
chunks.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.1 Cancellation Submission Process
chunks.text:
### 3.1 Cancellation Submission Process

Clients may initiate subscription cancellation via the CloudScale Admin Console (https://console.cloudscale.io/ billing) or by emailing written notice to billing@cloudscale.io. Cancellation notices must be received at least 48 hours prior to the next billing date.

output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments
output.text:
### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

output.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
output.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
output.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

output.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

inputs.query: Billing policy refund cancellation window and non-refundable fee structure for Enterprise subscriptions

output.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
output.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
output.text:
### 3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy

Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated refunds.

output.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
output.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.4 Non-Refundable Services
output.text:
### 3.4 Non-Refundable Services

The following professional fees and third-party expenses are strictly non-refundable under all circumstances:

- Custom Onboarding & Implementation: Dedicated deployment engineering, custom setup packages, and architecture consulting.
- Domain Registrations & SSL Certificates: Domain purchases, custom SSL certificate procurement, and DNS routing setup fees.
- Data Migration Engineering: Tailored database migration scripts, pipeline development, and dedicated engineering hours.
- Dedicated Technical Account Management (TAM): Monthly retainer fees for designated account managers.

output.header_path: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
output.section: 3. Cancellation & Refund Windows / 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
output.text:
### 3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee

CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:

- Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial service activation date.
- Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50 computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes strictly non-refundable.
- Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

Clients may initiate subscription cancellation via the CloudScale Admin Console (https://console.cloudscale.io/ billing) or by emailing written notice to billing@cloudscale.io. Cancellation notices must be received at least 48 hours prior to the next billing date.

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).", "score": 1.0, "retrieval_status": {"mode": "hybrid", "reranker": "disabled", "retrieval_ms": 427.90917699676356, "rerank_ms": 0}}, {"doc_id": "DOC-SLA-2024-V2", "version": "2.0", "effective_date": "January 15, 2024", "classification": "Public Customer Policy", "review_cycle": "Annual (Next Review: January 2025)", "target_audience": "Infrastructure, Database, API", "document_id": "DOC-SLA-2024-V2", "source_file": "sla_and_support_tier_policy.pdf", "file_path": "/app/data/documents/sla_and_support_tier_policy.pdf", "source_sha256": "2c93557b69844d601db9053781f39c56b30ef995827c9aae9d3fb5fbadb7a17e", "header_path": "4. Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$
